Calcium homeostasis: vitamin D increases gut absorption; PTH raises and calcitonin lowers serum Ca²⁺.
Bone remodeling: sites of action of antiresorptive (estrogen, bisphosphonates, calcitonin) and anabolic (PTH, teriparatide) agents.
Osteopenia        -    clin hip/vertebral frx       -    T-score ≤ −2.5 at spine/femoral neck/total hip/33% radius      -    T-score −1 to −2.5 w/ high 10-yr frx probability
very high = anabolic, romosozumab, (zoledronic ⍉ antireabsorb after) -> antiresorptive or bisphos or denosumab (if denosumab -> another antiresorptive - (⍉abrupt d/c))
Properly classify drug therapy as anabolic or antiresorptive (or as exhibiting properties of both).
Anabolic: teriparatide, abaloparatide        -     Antiresorptive: bisphosphonates, calcitonin, denosumab, estrogen/HRT, raloxifene      -    Both: romosozumab
bone formation: osteoblasts, osteoclasts, bone remodeling, bone resorption, bone formation, PTH, calcitonin, sclerostin.
Osteoblasts: bone-forming cells        -     Osteoclasts: bone-resorbing cells                    -    bone remodeling: cont process of bone resorb (osteoclasts) THEN bone form (osteoblasts)
bone resorb: bone breakdown via osteoclast -> release bone Ca into extracellular pool              -    bone form: osteoblast build new bone (modeling = bone form w.o prior resorb)

PTH: ↑extracell Ca: stim Ca reabsorb by renal tubules, ↓phosphate reabsorb, stim hydroxylation of vit D in kidneys, & ↑bone resorb by stim osteoclast activity (intermittent PTH favors form; cont PTH favors resorb)
Calcitonin: ↓extracellular Ca: inhibits bone resorb by inhibiting osteoclast activity
Sclerostin: inhibit osteoblast form from precursors, inhibit mature osteoblast function, inhibits new bone formation by modeling, and (to a lesser extent) ↓bone resorb
